name: Credit note and debit note
definition: A credit note or debit note under section 34 adjusts a supply already invoiced. Rule 53(1A) fixes nine particulars, (a) to (i). Clause (b) requires the nature of the document, and clause (g) requires the serial number(s) and date(s) of every invoice or bill of supply it adjusts — plural, because one note may cover several.
why_it_exists: It is the only lawful way to change the taxable value or the tax on a supply after the invoice. An adjustment posted without one is an adjustment with no document behind it.
inputs: the invoices or bills of supply being adjusted
whether the note is a credit note or a debit note
outputs: the set of rule 53(1A) particulars found
the set of mandatory particulars absent
preconditions: a tax invoice or bill of supply has already been issued for the supply
exceptions: rule 54(5) extends the rule 54(2) and 54(4) relaxations to documents issued under rule 53
common_mistakes: inferring the direction from the amount sign instead of reading clause (b), the nature of the document
linking a note to one invoice when clause (g) is plural and the note may adjust several
confusing it with a refund voucher, which reverses an advance where no supply was made
confusing it with a revised tax invoice, which re-documents supplies made before the registration certificate was issued
legal_references: UNKNOWN — section 34 of the CGST Act, which fixes WHEN a credit or debit note may be issued and its time limits, is a different document and was not read for this record
icai_references: UNKNOWN — the accounting period in which a credit note is recognised is a separate question from its GST particulars
gst_references: UNKNOWN — source is the Rules as at 01-01-2022; later amendments not held locally
evidence_required: the adjusted taxable value and tax
confidence_factors: weak when the nature of the document is not stated, because credit and debit run in opposite directions
weak when a referenced invoice cannot be located
validation_checks: all nine particulars (a) to (i) are present
clause (b) states whether the document is a credit note or a debit note
clause (g) names at least one corresponding tax invoice or bill of supply
a debit note issued in pursuance of tax under section 74, 129 or 130 prominently carries INPUT TAX CREDIT NOT ADMISSIBLE
examples: a credit note naming invoices 21 and 22, stating the reduced taxable value, the rate and the tax credited to the recipient
counterexamples: a document that states an adjusted amount but not whether it is a credit or a debit — clause (b) fails
a debit note issued under section 74 without the INPUT TAX CREDIT NOT ADMISSIBLE marking — rule 53(3) fails

evidence.quote: A credit or debit note referred to in section 34 shall contain the following particulars
serial number(s) and date(s) of the corresponding tax invoice(s) or, as the case may be, bill(s) of supply;
